subject: giraffe
pitch: A young reticulated giraffe. Chestnut patches outlined by bright cream lines all over its body and neck, a short mane of stiff brown hair down the neck, two fuzzy ossicones with black tufts on top, big ears, long lashes, a long dark tongue just peeking out, and slender legs fading to cream above the hooves.
reasoning:
I'm planning out realistic giraffe proportions, aiming for a young giraffe around 2.8 meters tall, and sketching the overall ellipsoid-based body shape for the model.

I'm figuring out the skeleton hierarchy now, placing joints for hips, spine, neck, and head, and defining a neck chain with polyline points running from chest to head base so the model has believable posture and articulation.

For the neck geometry I'm sweeping along the chain with a tapering elliptical radius, thinner at the top near the head, and setting up the base pattern coloring for the body before moving on to the mane.

For the mane itself I'm figuring out how to place small spike shapes along the dorsal side of the neck, which requires working out the neck's tangent direction and the opposite dorsal normal so the spikes point away from the curve correctly.

Spike base can take a ChainPoint directly, so I can walk along the neck chain and place spikes using a fixed back-of-neck direction vector, with a dark brown color for the mane.

For positioning on the neck's surface rather than the centerline, I need to offset each base point outward using the frame's up/back directions to account for the neck radius, using moved() with weighted dorsal offsets. Next I'll add small ossicones on the head using capsule or spike shapes.

For the head, I'm planning a joint at the top of the neck for a boxy skull shape, with the muzzle as a sphere, eyes with thin lash details, ears as capsules or slabs, ossicones with capsule shapes topped by dark tuft spheres, and a dark tongue peeking from the mouth. The mouth needs separate upper skull and lower jaw joints, with the jaw holding the tongue and positioned at the mouth location.

For legs, I'm setting up four chains with hip/knee/hock joints, naming them foreL, foreR, hindL, hindR with a "leg" role for each.

Now I'm working out leg joint positions down to hoof tips, settling on four points per leg (thigh, knee, ankle, hoof) so each span gets a clear joint name, then sweeping the geometry with tapering radius from thick at the hip to thin at the ankle, painted with a gradient color, and adding small dark brown hoof caps at the tips.

For the body, I'm planning a cream base coat with reticulated chestnut patches separated by cream gap lines, using varied chestnut shades for natural variation. I'm shaping the torso with a loft across several stations from rump to chest, adjusting width and height at each point to get the giraffe's body silhouette.

For the neck, I'm sweeping along the chain with a tapering radius function, then figuring out the mane placement by estimating the tangent direction along the neck's path so I can position the dorsal ridge spikes correctly on the back of the neck.

I'm now setting up roughly 14 brown mane spikes positioned along the neck using the computed dorsal offset, then moving on to figure out the head joint and ossicone placement based on the neck tip's orientation.

Attaching head geometry parts directly to the head bone, using a stylized elongated skull box and muzzle built from scaled spheres rather than plain boxes for a more rounded giraffe shape.

Now I'm adding a jaw joint hinged below the head, placing a lower jaw box on that bone, and sweeping a thin rod shape for the tongue so it hangs forward from the mouth, both rigged to the jaw joint by name reference.

Next I'm positioning the eyes on the sides of the skull with dark spheres, adding small angled boxes for lashes above each eye, and considering a tiny white highlight sphere for shine. Then I'm working out ear placement — long pointed giraffe ears set sideways-back on the head, building them as a slab shape from a set of outline points in 3D space.

For ossicones, I'm sketching them as capsules rising from the skull topped with small dark sphere tufts, giving them a lighter brown base color with darker tips, then moving on to think about the stiff brown mane made of short spikes.

Now I'm working out the four-leg chain setup, placing hip joints at front and back of the body with knee, ankle, and hoof points forming a straight polyline so each chain gets three spans, parented to the root joint with a "leg" role. I'm also figuring out how the leg sweep radius should taper as a function of position along the chain, moving from thicker near the hip to thinner toward the hoof.

Then I'm defining a vertical gradient paint for the legs that blends cream below the knee into a patched chestnut color above it, using a single direction vector so it applies consistently across all four legs.

For hooves, I'm attaching a small cylinder part to the last joint of each leg chain, tapering slightly wider at the bottom to form the hoof shape.

Working through the rest of the giraffe build—ears, muzzle, eyes, tongue, mane spikes, ossicones, tail, and leg sweeps—I'm mapping out the joint hierarchies, paint gradients for patches, and part placements so each piece attaches rigidly to the right bone with sensible colors and sizes, aiming for a stylized young reticulated giraffe standing naturally on the ground plane.
